data.title: Journey of Water
data.introduction: Discover the amazing ways that moisture travels around our planet every single day.

terms.definition: The process where liquid turns into a gas when it gets warm.
terms.exampleSentence: Sunlight causes rapid evaporation of puddles on the sidewalk after a storm.
terms.clozeSentence: We watched the puddle disappear through evaporation as the sun heated the concrete.
terms.scenario: A wet shirt is hung on a clothesline in the bright sun and slowly dries out because the wetness goes into the air.

terms.definition: The change of a gas back into tiny liquid droplets when it cools down.
terms.exampleSentence: Cold glasses of lemonade often develop condensation on the outside.
terms.clozeSentence: Droplets formed on the cold soda can due to condensation in the warm room.
terms.scenario: Tiny water drops appear on the bathroom mirror after someone takes a hot steamy shower.

terms.definition: Any form of moisture that falls from the sky toward the ground.
terms.exampleSentence: Heavy rain and snow are common types of winter precipitation.
terms.clozeSentence: Dark storm clouds brought freezing precipitation that covered the yard in white flakes.
terms.scenario: Children look out the classroom window as soft white flakes begin to drift down from the gray clouds.

terms.definition: The gathering of fallen moisture into large bodies like rivers, lakes, and oceans.
terms.exampleSentence: Streams carry runoff downhill for the final collection in the ocean.
terms.clozeSentence: Rainwater flowed down the hills into a large lake for its collection.
terms.scenario: Streams of rainwater run off the street and pool together into a big puddle at the corner.

terms.definition: The invisible gas state of a liquid floating freely in the air.
terms.exampleSentence: Hot water creates invisible vapor that rises toward the kitchen ceiling.
terms.clozeSentence: Steam from the boiling kettle turned into warm vapor in the kitchen air.
terms.scenario: You can see your breath turn into a little puff of steam on a very cold winter morning.

terms.definition: A series of steps or events that happen over and over again in the same order.
terms.exampleSentence: The seasons follow a predictable cycle throughout the entire year.
terms.clozeSentence: Water moves in a never-ending cycle from the ground to the sky and back again.
terms.scenario: A caterpillar turns into a chrysalis, becomes a butterfly, lays eggs, and the whole pattern begins again.
